title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government is responding to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its stance on how AI should be regulated and used in the public sector. It highlights key commitments and actions aimed at improving transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its strategy for regulating artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, focusing on ensuring fairness, reliability, and security in exams. The approach involves setting safeguards, monitoring AI tools, and collaborating with the education, science, and business ministries to support the sector's integrity.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report explores how the use of copyrighted material in training and developing AI systems can affect creators, consumers, and the broader industry, identifying legal risks and potential benefits. It offers recommendations for safeguards and best practices that aim to balance innovation with respect for intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a formal reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, recognising the urgent need to tackle the social, economic and ethical impacts of artificial intelligence in the UK. It outlines a strategy to strengthen research, boost industry innovation, improve regulatory frameworks, and build public trust while keeping the UK at the forefront of AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, including guidelines for meetings and decision-making. It also provides a set of frequently asked questions to help participants understand the review process and key terms.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence, sharing its perspective on how AI should be regulated. In the submission, the CSPL outlines key recommendations and highlights potential risks and policy considerations for responsible AI governance.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence reshapes the regulation of medical products and sets out how the AI White Paper principles will be applied. It aims to balance safety, effectiveness, and innovation by establishing clear guidelines for AI‑enabled medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy seeks to position our defence organisation as the world’s leading AI‑capable entity among similarly sized forces, focusing on effectiveness, efficiency, trustworthiness, and influence. It outlines a vision for developing and deploying AI technologies that strengthen our strategic capabilities while maintaining high standards of reliability and public confidence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI’s benefits while addressing associated risks. It aims to guide the implementation of AI technologies, ensuring safety, security, and regulatory compliance while promoting innovation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyrighted works are currently being used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, summarising the progress made and the challenges encountered. It offers findings, recommendations, and next steps for policymakers to guide future regulation and practice.
